title: China Entrenches AI Competition
text:
China Entrenches AI Competition

Tilly Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 27 Jul 2026

China’s latest surprisingly good artificial intelligence model, Kimi K3 from Moonshot AI, has shocked industry leaders and politicians on both sides of the Pacific. Moonshot as a company is only three years old, but it has managed to build a model that is nearly as powerful as the most advanced US models, while being open for users to download and modify. Beyond that technical accomplishment, though, what’s important is how Moonshot and other Chinese AI developers have ensured that open-weight models will be a significant part of the AI market into the future. That will mean ongoing competitive pressure on closed models from the US leaders Anthropic and OpenAI.The success of open models is not an outcome that was obvious from the beginning of Chinese companies’ AI push. When Chinese developers first began opening up their models, it was more a forced choice than a farsighted strategy. US models had started out well ahead, and the Chinese models could not compete with their performance at the frontier, so being cheaper and open-weight was the main way they could attract users. (Most AI models are not truly “open source,” because not all of the materials and processes used to create the model are published; “open weight” means a model and its parameters can be downloaded, run locally and modified.)
